one_month_reasoning: Q3 2026 results should come around mid-November (Q2 was Aug 5; last year's Q3 came in early-to-mid November), so probably after Oct 31. Items that could land in the window: the launch or pricing of the ~$3.5B Kentucky leveraged loan / high-yield financing (a clean print would help; wide pricing or a delay would hurt), the CB-4 delivery (168 MW, guided 2H26), progress on closing the Abernathy sale and Chesapeake, and bitcoin/AI-infrastructure sentiment. Short-horizon signals cut both ways. Momentum is negative: down ~13% in the week to Sep 28, steady Form 4 insider sales from the CEO and a director, and the stock is ~50% below its 52-week high. Against that, short interest is ~29% of float, which can drive sharp rallies. With no scheduled earnings, I centre at ~$14.75 (a slight negative tilt for momentum and insider supply) with ~26% monthly vol (91%/3.5).

fair_value.method: Blend of a contracted-cash-flow DCF ($7.9 at the horizon; 10% WACC, 80% margin, $6.0B remaining capex, 1% terminal growth), 12x 2028E EBITDA of $1.38B less $8.1B end-2027 net debt ($13.9), and an 8% cap-rate NAV plus pipeline option ($16.5), weighted 40/30/30 across 609M diluted shares.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Unlevered FCF Q4'26-2036 from contracted leases only: revenue ~$0.70B 2027, ~$1.44B 2028, $1.73B 2029+; 80% EBITDA margin; capex $1.2B/$3.3B/$1.5B (Q4'26/27/28); 3% maintenance capex; taxes from 2030; WACC 10%; terminal growth 1%. EV $6.4B (TV is $5.0B of it) - $2.7B net debt + $0.53B Abernathy = $4.2B, or $6.90/share today, rolled forward 12 months at ~15% cost of equity = $7.9. Sensitivities: WACC 9% -> $9.2 today; 85% margin -> $8.1; Anthropic slips 1 year -> $5.9.

bear.story: The AI-infrastructure trade de-rates, or stress at Fluidstack or Anthropic (Fluidstack gets ~80%+ of its contracted revenue from Anthropic, and Google's backstop covers only $3.2B of the $6.7B Lake Mariner leases) makes the market price WULF on contracted cash flow at a high discount rate. Other routes here: the Kentucky financing prices wide or needs equity at a low price, or Justified slips into late 2028. Equity is then near the DCF value of $6-8.

base.story: CB-4 and CB-5 arrive on schedule and the Kentucky debt closes at roughly high-single-digit cost. The stock trades at ~11-12x 2028 EBITDA after more modest dilution (equity or converts to fund Muskie). Headline-driven swings continue, and the tail of insider selling and the high short interest offset each other.

bull.story: A new 250-500 MW lease (e.g. Muskie) with a hyperscaler or IG-backed tenant, together with strong AI capex sentiment, re-rates WULF toward data-center-platform multiples (16-18x forward EBITDA) and toward the ~$33 analyst consensus. A short squeeze adds to the move.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$8 the market is valuing equity at or below my contracted-only DCF ($6.9 today, $7.9 rolled forward). That means it is pricing a real impairment of the contracts or the financing (Fluidstack/Anthropic credit stress, a failed or punitive Kentucky financing, a major construction delay or cost overrun at Justified, or heavy dilution), not ordinary volatility in a 91%-vol stock.

key_uncertainties: End-tenant concentration: Anthropic directly ($19B) and through Fluidstack (most of the $6.7B Lake Mariner leases) makes up nearly all of ~$27B contracted revenue; Google's backstop covers $3.2B
Discount rate on contracted cash flow: each 1pp of WACC moves the DCF ~$2.3/share; the market seems to use ~8% while my DCF uses 10%
Construction execution and cost at Justified (401 MW at $10-12M/MW) and the terms of the $3.5B financing
Dilution: Google warrants (~74M shares), RSUs, three convertible series, and likely further equity to fund the 250-500 MW/yr growth target
Lease escalators and renewal terms are not disclosed; Lake Mariner's 10-year terms create re-leasing risk around 2036
Real NOI margin: 70% (Abernathy disclosure) vs the 85% target
reasoning: WULF is now a construction-stage AI data-center landlord. It has ~$27B of contracted lease revenue: Lake Mariner leases to Fluidstack/Core42 of ~$0.78B/yr by 2027, and a 20-year Anthropic lease at Justified of ~$0.95B/yr from 2028. Against that sit $5.7B of debt, $3.0B of cash, ~$6B of remaining build capex, and 609M diluted shares once Google's warrants and RSUs are counted. Reported losses are dominated by warrant mark-to-market ($756M in Q2) and are not cash, but H1'26 free cash flow was -$1.5B. Skeptic findings: (1) almost all contracted revenue traces back to one AI lab, Anthropic, directly or through Fluidstack, which has ~$660M revenue, owns no chips and depends on Google's backstop and Anthropic demand (Substack and TechTimes); (2) credit is BB/Ba2, and debt costs rise with a 5.29% 10-year Treasury; (3) dilution keeps coming (a $900M equity raise at $19, the convertible series, the Google warrants); (4) insiders are steady net sellers (CEO and director sales in Aug-Sep), though the amounts are small next to the CEO's ~40M shares; (5) short interest is ~29% of float. Against these, the contracts and the backstop are real, and the analyst consensus is ~$33. My contracted-only DCF at a 10% WACC gives only ~$6.9 today ($7.9 at the horizon). It is very sensitive to the discount rate: the market's ~$9B equity value implies roughly an 8% cap rate on 2028 NOI plus credit for the pipeline. A 12x EV/EBITDA method gives $13.9 and an 8%-cap NAV with the pipeline gives $16.5. The 40/30/30 blend is $12.3, ~17% below the price. For the distribution I use a lognormal with median ~$12.8, nudged above fair value for the short-squeeze and pipeline optionality, and sigma 0.75 (below the 91% realized vol because part of that is sentiment noise that should not compound fully over a year). That gives P(>= $14.91) ~0.42 and fat tails both ways, consistent with scenarios of $6 / $13.5 / $27 at 30/45/25%. Research limits: Twelve Data fundamentals and estimates were behind a paywall, Alpha Vantage was rate-limited, and SEC EDGAR blocks curl without a contact User-Agent, so filings were read through WebFetch. I found no published short-seller report on WULF.
